stem: Seven observations are arranged in ascending order: 12, 18, 24, 31, 39, 45, 52. What is the median of this data set?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Selecting the 3rd value (position (7-1)/2 = 3) instead of the correct (n+1)/2 = 4th position gives 24.
For n = 7 (odd), median is at position (7+1)/2 = 4. The 4th value in the ordered set is 31.
Computing the arithmetic mean of all seven values (sum = 221, mean = 221/7 = 31.57) and confusing it with the median, or averaging the 4th and 5th values (31 + 39)/2 = 35 as if n were even.
Selecting the 5th value (position n/2 + 1 = 5 using an incorrect even-n formula) gives 39.

explanation: For an odd number of ordered observations, median = value at position (n+1)/2. Here n = 7, so median position = (7+1)/2 = 4. Counting along: 12 (1st), 18 (2nd), 24 (3rd), 31 (4th). Median = 31.

explanation_sections.punchline: For odd n, the middle position is (n+1)/2 - there is no averaging of two values.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify the distribution and model: median for ungrouped odd-count data. Formula: median = x_{(n+1)/2}. n = 7, position = 4. Read off the 4th value from the sorted list: 31.
explanation_sections.lesson: The even-n formula averages two middle values; the odd-n formula picks a single middle value at position (n+1)/2. Never average adjacent values when n is odd.
explanation_sections.timing: 10-15 seconds. Count to position 4 in the sorted sequence immediately.
